Dear Neighbors,

I’m writing to address concerns about the drone I flew from the roof deck at Larkspur Lofts on Saturday, October 31, around 4 p.m., and to clarify what I was doing.

I’m Jess Okafor in Unit 5A, and I’ve lived here for three years. I work as a wedding photographer and was testing a new drone, a Halvard Mini 4, before photographing a vineyard wedding in Dundee. The flight lasted approximately 11 minutes. Throughout the flight, the camera was pointed west toward the river and the Fremont Bridge—not toward residents’ windows.

I understand that seeing and hearing a drone hovering over the courtyard, without knowing why it was there, could be unsettling. I’m sorry that my flight caused worry. I should have considered how it would look to neighbors and communicated beforehand.

Anyone who would like to see what was recorded is welcome to view the full, unedited footage. Please knock on my door at 5A or email me at jess.okafor@mailbox.example, and we can arrange a time.

I also want to address the note posted in the lobby. It identified my unit and called me a “creep.” While I understand the privacy concerns behind it, publicly identifying and insulting a neighbor is not an acceptable way to raise them. Seeing that posted in our shared space felt deeply personal and upsetting.

Our current HOA rules do not address drones, but that does not mean residents’ concerns should go unaddressed. I will not fly from the roof again until the board decides on a rule. I will ask that the issue be added to the November 19 board meeting agenda, at 7 p.m. in the community room.

If something I do causes concern, please speak with me directly rather than posting a note. I’m willing to listen, answer questions, and work toward clear expectations that respect everyone’s privacy and comfort.

Sincerely,  
Jess Okafor  
Unit 5A
